args.body:
Hi Dora! I just had a look at your personal website at www.dora-website.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What works:
- It's clean and loads instantly — no clutter, no pop-ups, no autoplay. That's a genuine plus.
- The page tells the reader right away what the site is (a personal site) and how to reach you (dora@securemail-hub.com). Simple and direct.

What could be better:
- The site is currently just one line of text, so there's very little for a visitor to actually engage with. Even a short intro paragraph about who you are and what you do would give people a reason to stay.
- Consider adding a few sections — for example an "About" page, a portfolio or projects list, and links to your other profiles (GitHub, LinkedIn, etc.).
- A bit of visual personality would help it feel like *your* space rather than a placeholder: some color, a photo, or a short bio.
- If you do add more pages, a simple navigation menu or footer with your contact details would make it easier to browse.

Overall it's a nice, tidy starting point — the foundation is solid, it just needs a little more content and personality to really shine. Happy to give more specific suggestions if you tell me what kind of site you're aiming for!

Best,
Emma Johnson

Hi Eve! I just had a look at your blog at www.eve-blog.com and wanted to share some feedback.

What works:
- The site is clean and lightweight — it loads fast and there's nothing distracting from the content.
- Leading with a personal detail like hiking gives the blog a clear, warm personality and a nice theme to build on.

What could be better:
- Right now the blog is a single line, so there's no actual reading experience yet. Publishing a few posts would make it feel like a real blog.
- Since hiking is your favorite hobby, it could be a great organizing theme — trail write-ups, gear notes, trip planning tips, photos from the trail. That gives readers a reason to subscribe.
- Adding a small "About" section and a way to contact you or subscribe to new posts would help turn casual visitors into regulars.
- Photos and a bit of visual styling would make a hiking blog really shine — even a simple header image and consistent post layout goes a long way.
- A tag or category system would help once you have more than a handful of posts.

Overall, a lovely starting point with a charming personal touch — it just needs a few real posts and some imagery to bring it to life. I'd love to read it once it's up!

Best,
Emma Johnson
